Summer Solstice: The Longest Ride

The summer solstice — around June 21st — delivers the most daylight hours of the year. In Scotland, the sun rises before 4:30am and sets after 10pm, giving 17-18 hours of light. In England, you get 16+ hours. For motorcyclists, it's an invitation for the ultimate dawn-to-dusk ride.

The Dawn-to-Dusk Challenge

The concept is simple: start riding at sunrise, finish at sunset. With 16-18 hours of light, you can cover serious distance — or ride a modest route at an incredibly leisurely pace. Both approaches are rewarding.

  • Distance approach: Ride 400-500 miles in a day. Land's End to John o' Groats is theoretically possible in the longest daylight, though we'd recommend something more scenic.
  • Scenic approach: Ride 200-250 miles on the best roads you can find, stopping frequently for photos, coffee, and appreciation. Quality over quantity.

Solstice Ride Ideas

Scotland: The Midnight Ride

  • In the far north of Scotland, it barely gets dark around the solstice. Ride through the midsummer twilight — a unique and atmospheric experience.
  • Route: Inverness → NC500 west coast section → Durness → watch the midnight sky

England: Coast to Coast

  • Ride from the east coast sunrise to the west coast sunset.
  • Route: Whitby (sunrise) → North York Moors → Yorkshire Dales → Lake District → St Bees (sunset)

Wales: Mountain Marathon

  • Link every major Welsh mountain pass in a single day.
  • Route: Horseshoe Pass → Snowdonia passes → Aberystwyth → Devil's Bridge → Black Mountain Pass → Gospel Pass

Practical Tips

  • Start with a full tank and plan fuel stops carefully
  • Eat well — you'll need sustained energy for a long riding day
  • Dress in layers — dawn can be cold even in June, midday warm, and evening cool again
  • Take breaks every 90 minutes minimum to stay sharp
  • Apply sunscreen — all-day sun exposure on a motorcycle causes significant sunburn
The summer solstice ride is a celebration of motorcycling's core appeal — freedom, daylight, and the open road. Whether you ride 100 miles or 500, the solstice reminds us that the longest days are the best days.

Route Planning for Maximum Daylight

To fully maximise your solstice riding day, plan your route to exploit every available minute of usable light. Start at an east-facing viewpoint to witness the sunrise, ride progressively westward through the long day, and finish at a west-facing location for the sunset. This natural east-to-west progression keeps the light working in your favour throughout the entire ride and creates a deeply satisfying narrative arc from dawn through midday to dusk.

In the far north of Scotland, the midsummer sun barely sets at all around the solstice period. Near Durness and Cape Wrath, the sky glows continuously through the brief twilight hours between sunset and sunrise, creating an eerie, hauntingly beautiful light quality that is completely unique to the northern midsummer. Riding through this perpetual twilight is a profound and memorable experience — the familiar landscape takes on an otherworldly, dreamlike quality that you will not find at any other time of the year.
keyTakeaways: The summer solstice around 21 June is the longest day, with up to 18 hours of usable light in northern Scotland.
Plan an east-to-west route: start at an east-facing sunrise viewpoint and finish at a west-facing sunset spot.
In the far north near Durness and Cape Wrath the sun barely sets, creating continuous midsummer twilight.
Take a break every 90 minutes on a long solstice ride to stay sharp, and apply sunscreen against all-day sun.
The solstice is the peak of daylight, so make the most of it before the days begin to shorten again.

faq.q: When is the summer solstice in 2026?
faq.a: The summer solstice falls around 21 June, marking the longest day of the year. Daylight ranges from about 16.5 hours in southern England to over 18 hours in northern Scotland, giving riders the maximum possible window for a dawn-to-dusk ride. After the solstice, the days gradually begin to shorten again.

faq.q: How should I plan a solstice route?
faq.a: Exploit every minute of light with an east-to-west progression. Start at an east-facing viewpoint for sunrise, ride steadily westward through the long day, and finish at a west-facing location for sunset. This keeps the light working in your favour and creates a satisfying arc from dawn through midday to dusk.

faq.q: What is special about the far north at the solstice?
faq.a: Near Durness and Cape Wrath in the far north of Scotland, the midsummer sun barely sets at all. The sky glows continuously through the brief twilight between sunset and sunrise, giving an eerie, dreamlike light quality found nowhere else in Britain. Riding through this perpetual twilight is a profound and memorable experience.

faq.q: How do I stay safe on a long solstice ride?
faq.a: Fatigue is the main risk when you are tempted to ride for 15 hours or more. Take a proper break at least every 90 minutes to stay sharp, eat and hydrate regularly, and apply sunscreen, as all-day sun exposure on a motorcycle causes significant sunburn without you feeling the heat. Do not chase every last minute of light if you are tired.
